quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A sharp turn is ahead. Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sharp turn is ahead. Slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that a sharp turn is coming and you should reduce your speed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Stop only if other cars are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycles cross here.
questions.explanation: This sign shows where bicycles cross or ride next to traffic. Drive slowly and carefully in this area because bicycles regularly pass through.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, what is important to remember?

options.text: The road is very slippery right when rain starts.
You need extra space to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are dangerous and slippery, especially when rain just starts. Your tires travel on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down in heavy rain or when water is standing on the road to keep your wheels from slipping.

questions.question: How should you adjust a seat belt?

options.text: Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Loose enough to turn off the warning light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should sit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable. You should be able to fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When a child is about to run into the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a child is about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who do not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night compared to signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no train in sight or sound, you must stop if:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop before railroad tracks if red lights are flashing, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible and close. When in doubt, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey first?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer.
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions come before signs, lights, and road markings. Police officers, fire police, highway workers, and school crossing guards can direct traffic.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pull to the right side of the road and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, create a clear path for the emergency vehicle. Slow down and pull safely to the side of the road and stop. In heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is going up or down?

options.text: Yes, if a train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle will not damage the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways first.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, down gates, and bells mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never go around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: What might happen when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: Both the alcohol and drug effects may become stronger.
Both the alcohol and drug effects may become weaker.
Only the alcohol effect may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the alcohol and drug effects may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, having one drink while taking a cold medicine can affect you like you had several drinks.

questions.question: A driver taking over-the-counter medicine should:

options.text: Drive anyway, even if there are warnings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label before driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medicines can make driving unsafe. Always check the label for warnings, even for cold or allergy medicine. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive.

questions.question: When driving in school zones, you should:

options.text: Never drive faster than 10 miles per hour.
Expect students to let vehicles go first.
Drive the same speed during school hours and when school is closed.
Follow the posted school zone speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the posted school zone speed limit.
questions.explanation: Follow the posted speed limits in school zones. Breaking school zone speed limits has stronger penalties.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol at a social event, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Get a ride home with someone who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with someone who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The safest way to avoid impaired driving is to arrange a ride with a sober friend. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your blood. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns.
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed. Do not turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: To stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and back. Avoid driving next to them and do not follow too closely behind them.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your ability to focus on the road.
Lowering your chances of an accident.
Making you fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your ability to focus on the road.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect how well you drive. You may not drive safely if you are worried, excited, scared, angry, or sad. Stress reduces your focus on driving. It is better to wait before driving than to drive when emotionally upset.

questions.question: About half of all motorcycle crashes:
questions.correctAnswerText: Involve another vehicle.
questions.explanation: About half of all motorcycle crashes involve another vehicle. Watch for motorcycles around you, especially in bad weather and when changing lanes or turning.

questions.question: When you see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Speed up to prevent traffic backup.
Move to another lane, if safe, to make room for entering traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if safe, to make room for entering traffic.
questions.explanation: When on a road with two or more lanes, make space for vehicles entering. If no one is next to you, move to another lane.

questions.question: When facing an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Show them you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is driving dangerously toward you, stay calm and create distance between your vehicles. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: How should you make room for vehicles entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down quickly to let them in.
Always drive in the far left lane.
Safely move to the next lane to give them space.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely move to the next lane to give them space.
questions.explanation: Usually drive in the right or center lane. When a car is entering from a ramp, safely move to the next lane. During rush hour, avoid the right lane to make room for more cars entering the freeway.

questions.question: What should you do before starting the car?

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting the car, buckle your seat belt and check that all passengers do the same.

questions.question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: What should you do when you see emergency vehicles with flashing lights coming toward you from behind?

options.text: Speed up to stay away from the emergency vehicle.
Slow down but do not stop.
Move to the curb or edge of the road and stop right away.
Keep driving and turn on your hazard lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the curb or edge of the road and stop right away.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or a siren, move to the nearest curb or edge of the road and stop. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
Move your eyes from side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, stop regularly. Rest and stretch your body, even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal.
questions.explanation: Before turning, turn on your signal three to four seconds ahead of time.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A road is joining from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
You may not see the turn signals.
You may not see the brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car in front slows or stops suddenly, you may not have enough time to stop and could hit it.

questions.question: When pulled over by police, what documents must a driver show?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When pulled over, you must show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You must carry all three documents whenever you drive.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights warn of dangerous intersections. Treat them the same way you treat stop signs.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: You have had an upsetting incident at work. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
questions.explanation: If you are angry or upset, take time to calm down before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: A driver who drives much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Should not let following cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic can be dangerous. If you drive slowly on a two-lane road and cars back up behind you, you must pull over and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
Drivers checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers maintaining a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for road conditions. Always drive within the speed limit and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention away from driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel is a distraction.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other cars are nearby.
Signal only if other cars are visible.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other cars are nearby.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from the curb. Do not skip signaling—it is the law.

questions.question: You cannot pass:

options.text: When a school bus has stopped to load passengers.
On hills where you cannot see ahead clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass within 100 feet of an intersection unless a sign allows it. Do not pass on hills, curves, or where you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass a stopped school bus.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: This warning sign is yellow and black. It tells you that a lane is ending and you need to merge safely with other traffic.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic.
May drive through if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you may drive through the intersection if it is clear. You may also turn right or left unless a sign prevents it. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians when turning.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard ahead. Slow down and proceed carefully.
